mcqs.question: Which of the following best defines an inherited trait?

options.A: A characteristic that an organism acquires during its lifetime due to environmental influences.
options.B: A characteristic passed from parents to offspring through genetic material.
options.C: A characteristic that changes in an individual as it grows older.
options.D: A characteristic that is learned through observation of others.

mcqs.answer: A characteristic passed from parents to offspring through genetic material.
mcqs.explanation: Inherited traits are those transmitted from parents to offspring via genes. Option B correctly states this. Options A and C describe acquired or age‑related changes, while D describes learned behavior, none of which are inherited traits.

mcqs.question: A child learns to ride a bicycle by practicing daily, while his eye colour is brown like his mother’s. Which of the following correctly distinguishes the two traits?

options.A: Both eye colour and bicycle‑riding ability are inherited traits.
options.B: Eye colour is an inherited trait; bicycle‑riding ability is an acquired trait.
options.C: Bicycle‑riding ability is inherited; eye colour is acquired.

mcqs.answer: Eye colour is an inherited trait; bicycle‑riding ability is an acquired trait.
mcqs.explanation: Eye colour is determined by genes received from parents, making it an inherited trait. Riding a bicycle is learned through practice, an acquired trait. Hence option B is correct; the other options misclassify the traits.

mcqs.question: Consider two sets of offspring from the same parents: Set A shows a wide range of flower colours, while Set B shows almost identical flower colours. Which statement best explains the difference?

options.A: Set A exhibits greater genetic variation among offspring than Set B.
options.B: Set A has more acquired traits than Set B.
options.C: Set B has undergone mutation, reducing variation.
options.D: Both sets have the same level of variation; the observed difference is due to environmental factors.

mcqs.answer: Set A exhibits greater genetic variation among offspring than Set B.
mcqs.explanation: Variation refers to genetic differences among individuals. A wide range of flower colours indicates high genetic variation (Option A). Acquired traits (Option B) do not apply to flower colour, and mutation (Option C) would increase, not necessarily reduce, variation. Option D ignores the genetic basis of colour differences.

mcqs.question: Why is genetic variation considered crucial for the survival of a species in a changing environment?

options.A: It ensures that all individuals have identical traits, simplifying adaptation.
options.B: It provides a pool of different traits, increasing the chance that some individuals can survive new challenges.
options.C: It eliminates the need for natural selection.
options.D: It causes species to become extinct faster.

mcqs.answer: It provides a pool of different traits, increasing the chance that some individuals can survive new challenges.
mcqs.explanation: Genetic variation supplies diverse traits on which natural selection can act. When environments change, some variants may confer survival advantages, ensuring the species persists. Option B captures this; the other options are inaccurate statements about variation.
